title: Sam Parr's summary of the 22 Immutable Laws of Marketing: own a word, be first, be the opposite
summary: Sam Parr summarizes the book The 22 Immutable Laws of Marketing (which he rates 9/10) law by law. The core theme is positioning: win by being first in the customer's mind, owning one simple idea, sacrificing breadth, and defining yourself against the leader rather than copying them.

principles.text: Being first beats being better; if you can't be first, invent a new category you can lead.
principles.quote: It’s better to be first than it is to be better. The first brand in a customer’s mind almost always wins, regardless of product quality.

principles.text: Marketing is perception, not product: the best perceived product wins, not the best product.
principles.quote: Marketing is not about products…it’s about perceptions. The best product doesn’t win, the best perceived product does.

principles.text: Own one simple word or idea in the customer's mind; trying to mean many things means nothing.
principles.quote: Owning one simple word or idea in the customer’s mind is power. Brands that try to mean too many things mean nothing.

principles.text: If you're not the leader, don't copy them. Be the opposite to stand out.
principles.quote: If you’re not the leader, don’t copy them…be the opposite. That’s how you stand out.

principles.text: Winning requires saying no to customers, features and markets; stretching the brand across many products weakens it.
principles.quote: Winning requires saying no to customers, features, and markets. You have to give something up to stand for something.

principles.text: Discounting wins short-term but trains customers to never pay full price and damages the brand long-term.
principles.quote: Discounting boosts sales briefly, but eventually trains customers to never pay full price.
